arxiv-2205-07548.title: A Neuro-Symbolic ASP Pipeline for Visual Question Answering Thanks: This work was partially funded by the Bosch Center for Artificial Intelligence at Renningen, Germany.
arxiv-2205-07548.creator: THOMAS EITER, NELSON HIGUERA, JOHANNES OETSCH, MICHAEL PRITZ
arxiv-2205-07548.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by THOMAS EITER, NELSON HIGUERA, JOHANNES OETSCH, MICHAEL PRITZ. We present a neuro-symbolic visual question answering (VQA) pipeline for CLEVR, which is a well-known dataset that consists of pictures showing scenes with objects and questions related to them.

arxiv-2304-10081.title: Galaxy Morphology Classification Using Multi-Scale Convolution Capsule Network 2023 Galaxy Morphology Classification Using Multi-Scale Convolution Capsule Network – References
arxiv-2304-10081.creator: Guangping Li, Tingting Xu, Liping Li, Xianjun Gao, Zhijing Liu, Jie Cao, Mingcun Yang, Weihong Zhou
arxiv-2304-10081.description: Abstract The classification of galaxy morphology is a hot issue in astronomical research. Although significant progress has been made in the last decade in classifying galaxy morphology using deep learning technology, there are still some deficiencies in spatial feature representation and classification accuracy.

arxiv-2307-13649.title: Optoelectronic properties of silver doped copper oxide thin films
arxiv-2307-13649.creator: Vishal Mohade
arxiv-2307-13649.description: Abstract Abstract Thin films have found a wide variety of applications because of the substantial improvement in their properties as compared to bulk metals. Metal oxide thin films are increasingly being used in various fields and are especially important in functional applications.

arxiv-2402-14134.title: Bound states in the continuum in whispering gallery resonators with pointlike impurities
arxiv-2402-14134.creator: M.A. Figueroa, Vladimir Juričić, P.A. Orellana
arxiv-2402-14134.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by M.A. Figueroa, Vladimir Juričić, P.A. Orellana. Whispering-gallery resonators offer a versatile platform for manipulating the photonic transmission. Here, we study such a system, including periodically distributed pointlike impurities along the resonator with ring geometry. Based on an exact expression for the transmission probability we obtain here, we demonstrate that the bound states in the continuum (BICs) form from the whispering gallery modes at the high-symmetry momenta in the ring’s Brillouin zone.

arxiv-2403-05960.title: Unitary Friedberg–Jacquet periods and anticyclotomic p-adic L-functions
arxiv-2403-05960.creator: Andrew Graham
arxiv-2403-05960.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Andrew Graham. We extend the construction of the p p -adic L L -function interpolating unitary Friedberg–Jacquet periods in [ Gra21 ] to include the p p -adic variation of Maass–Shimura differential operators. In particular, we develop a theory of nearly overconvergent automorphic forms in higher degrees of coherent cohomology for unitary Shimura varieties generalising the results in [ GPR23 ] .

arxiv-2405-04709.title: Quillen’s Fundamental Spectral Sequences Revisited
arxiv-2405-04709.creator: Hossein Faridian
arxiv-2405-04709.description: Abstract . Quillen’s fundamental spectral sequences relate André-Quillen homology and cohomology to Tor and Ext functors. The five-term exact sequences arising from these spectral sequences are leveraged to characterize regular and complete intersection local rings. Despite their immense importance in the theory of André-Quillen homology and cohomology, these spectral sequences are not treated in the literature as they merit.

arxiv-2408-10244.title: Electric field dependent g factors of YbOH molecule
arxiv-2408-10244.creator: Alexander Petrov
arxiv-2408-10244.description: Abstract YbOH molecule is one of the most sensitive systems for the electron electric dipole moment ( e e EDM) searches. Zeeman splittings of the e e EDM sensitive levels have significant implications to control and suppress important systematic effects due to stray magnetic field in experiments for e e EDM searches.

arxiv-2504-04925.title: Scaling regimes in slow quenches within a gapped phase
arxiv-2504-04925.creator: Lakshita Jindal, Kavita Jain
arxiv-2504-04925.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lakshita Jindal, Kavita Jain. We consider the finite-time quench dynamics in the quantum transverse field Ising model which exhibits a second order phase transition from a paramagnetic to a ferromagnetic phase, as the transverse magnetic field is decreased.

arxiv-2505-19805.title: Translation-Equivariance of Normalization Layers and Aliasing in Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2505-19805.creator: Jérémy Scanvic, Quentin Barthélemy, Julián Tachella
arxiv-2505-19805.description: Abstract The design of convolutional neural architectures that are exactly equivariant to continuous translations is an active field of research. It promises to benefit scientific computing, notably by making existing imaging systems more physically accurate. Most efforts focus on the design of downsampling/pooling layers, upsampling layers and activation functions, but little attention is dedicated to normalization layers.

arxiv-2506-08116.title: The properties of primordially-seeded black holes and their hosts in the first billion years: implications for JWST
arxiv-2506-08116.creator: Pratika Dayal & Roberto Maiolino
arxiv-2506-08116.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pratika Dayal & Roberto Maiolino. James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations have opened a tantalising new window onto possible black holes as early as redshifts of z ∼ 10.4 z\sim 10.4 . arxiv-2509-15434.description: Abstract . Social media platforms are increasingly developing features that display crowdsourced context alongside posts, modeled after X’s Community Notes. These systems, which we term Crowdsourced Context Systems (CCS), have the potential to reshape our information ecosystem as major platforms embrace them as alternatives to top-down fact-checking.

arxiv-2601-20587.title: A Hybrid Jump–Diffusion Model for Coherent Optical Control of Quantum Emitters in hBN
arxiv-2601-20587.creator: Saifian Farooq Bhat, Michael K. Koch, Sachin Negi, Alexander Kubanek, Vibhav Bharadwaj, [0.5em] Department of Physics, Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati, India
arxiv-2601-20587.description: Abstract Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) has emerged as a promising two-dimensional host for stable single-photon emission owing to its wide bandgap, high photostability, and compatibility with nanophotonic integration. We present a simulation-based study of temperature-dependent spectral dynamics and optical coherence in a mechanically decoupled quantum emitter in hBN.

pmc-10649442.title: Nutritional Intervention in Cushing’s Disease: The Ketogenic Diet’s Effects on Metabolic Comorbidities and Adrenal Steroids
pmc-10649442.creator: Valentina Guarnotta, Roberta Amodei, Francesca Di Gaudio, Carla Giordano
pmc-10649442.description: Background: a very low-calorie ketogenic diet (VLCKD) is associated with improvement of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders. We aimed to evaluate the effects of a VLCKD in patients with Cushing’s disease (CD) as adjunctive therapy to treatment for the primary disease.

pmc-10710241.title: Clinical Complete Response After Conversion Therapy for Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Is Salvage Hepatectomy Necessary?
pmc-10710241.creator: Jia-Yi Wu, Jun-Yi Wu, De-Yi Liu, Han Li, Shao-Wu Zhuang, Bin Li, Jian-Yin Zhou, Jing-Yao Huang, Zhi-Bo Zhang, Shu-Qun Li, Mao-Lin Yan, Yao-Dong Wang
pmc-10710241.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to determine whether salvage hepatectomy offers prognostic advantages for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) patients with clinical complete response (cCR) after conversion therapy.MethodsA total of 74 consecutive uHCC patients with cCR after conversion therapy at seven major cancer centers in China between October 2018 and December 2021 were included.

pmc-11346100.title: Intestinal glucagon-like peptide-1: A new player associated with impaired counterregulatory responses to hypoglycaemia in type 1 diabetic mice
pmc-11346100.creator: Fang-Xin Jin, Yan Wang, Min-Ne Li, Ru-Jiang Li, Jun-Tang Guo
pmc-11346100.description: BACKGROUNDImpaired hypoglycaemic counterregulation has emerged as a critical concern for diabetic patients who may be hesitant to medically lower their blood glucose levels due to the fear of potential hypoglycaemic reactions. However, the patho-genesis of hypoglycaemic counterregulation is still unclear. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and its analogues have been used as adjunctive therapies for type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM).

pmc-11605076.title: Element-specific X-Ray detection of electron paramagnetic resonance in thin films of quantum bits
pmc-11605076.creator: Andrin Doll, Zhewen Xu, Vladyslav Romankov, Giovanni Boero, Stefano Rusponi, Harald Brune, Zaher Salman, Jan Dreiser
pmc-11605076.description: Element-specific magnetism accessible by synchrotron-based X-ray spectroscopy has proven to be valuable to study spin and orbital moments of transition metals and lanthanides in technologically relevant thin-film and monolayer samples. The access to coherent spin superposition states relevant for emergent quantum technologies remains, however, elusive with ordinary X-ray spectroscopy.

pmc-11622581.title: Advances in CAR-T cell therapy for hematologic and solid malignancies: latest updates from 2024 ESMO Congress
pmc-11622581.creator: Huageng Huang, Le Yu, Huawei Weng, Wei Zhang, Zhao Wang, Lin Wang, He Huang
pmc-11622581.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has emerged as one of the most rapidly evolving modalities of immunotherapy, with substantial success in the treatment of hematological malignancies and encouraging outcomes in solid tumors. Yet, the efficacy of CAR-T therapy is hindered by challenges such as suboptimal expansion and persistence, adverse events, a scarcity of ideal targets, high immunosuppression, and insufficient infiltration due to the intricate tumor microenvironment, all of which limit its application.

pmc-12524181.title: Unusual Epidemic of Tyzzer’s Disease in Commercial Rabbit Breeders: Clinical, Pathological, and Therapeutic Observations
pmc-12524181.creator: Benedetta Cordioli, Manuel Garbuio, Luca Palazzolo, Francesco Dorigo, Luca Zandonà, Laura Viel, Claudia Zanardello, Luca Bano, Librado Carrasco
pmc-12524181.description: Simple SummaryTyzzer’s disease is a bacterial infection caused by Clostridium piliforme. While described in various animal species, it remains an uncommon disease in commercial rabbitries today, particularly in breeders. The clinical presentation and gross pathology may be variable and mislead the diagnosis towards other more common bacterial infections.

pmc-12596144.title: In silico analysis of insect-associated bacterial phytases reveals optimal biochemical properties and function in poultry gut condition
pmc-12596144.creator: Olyad Erba Urgessa, Ketema Tafess Tulu, Mesfin Tafesse Gemeda, Hunduma Dinka, Michael DeGiorgio
pmc-12596144.description: MotivationInsect guts may harbor phytase-producing bacteria applicable in poultry nutrition, but only Serratia sp. TN49 and its histidine acid phytase (AEQ29498.1) have been studied for this purpose. Therefore, AEQ29498.1 was used as a query to conduct a homology search for insect-associated bacterial phytases, followed by prediction of their structure and function.

pmc-12637207.title: A novel method for evaluating and visualizing scratch wound healing assays using level-set and image sector analysis
pmc-12637207.creator: Markéta Vašinková, Michal Krumnikl, Arootin Gharibian, Ondřej Mičulek, Eva Kriegová, Petr Gajdoš, Derek Abbott
pmc-12637207.description: Scratch wound healing assays are widely used to study collective cell migration, essential for understanding tissue regeneration, drug effects, and wound healing mechanisms. However, conventional analyses often rely on wound edge dynamics or individual cell tracks, limiting spatial insight into migration behavior.

pmc-12752159.title: Mature NK-cell lymphoma presenting with chylothorax and delirium: a rare emergency case
pmc-12752159.creator: Wen Shang, Zhiguo Guo, Qingbian Ma, Jijun Wang, Yuchang Xu
pmc-12752159.description: BackgroundExtranodal natural killer (NK)/T-cell lymphomas constitute less than 1% of non-Hodgkin lymphomas, with central nervous system involvement and chylothorax representing exceptionally rare presentations. This unique combination has not been previously reported in emergency medicine literature.Case presentationA previously healthy 51-year-old Chinese male presented with progressive dyspnea, high fever, and bilateral pleural effusion over eight days.

pmc-12840571.title: Sutureless‐dehydrated amniotic membrane (Omnigen®) mounted on contact lens (OmniLenz®) in the treatment of small corneal perforations secondary to exposure keratitis in ICU patients
pmc-12840571.creator: Nancy M. Lotfy, Mubarak Alrasheedi, Rola Y. Khachaba, Hamad Alshatti, Yousef Taleb Ali
pmc-12840571.description: Background:Exposure keratopathy is a common ocular complication in patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) and may progress from superficial epithelial breakdown to corneal perforation, a vision-threatening emergency requiring timely management. Conventional treatments often necessitate urgent surgery, which is challenging in critically ill individuals who are unsuitable for surgical intervention.

pmc-13178181.title: A plain language summary of the PERSEUS study of daratumumab plus bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone for treating newly diagnosed multiple myeloma
pmc-13178181.creator: Pieter Sonneveld, Meletios A. Dimopoulos, Mario Boccadoro, Hang Quach, P. Joy Ho, Meral Beksac, Cyrille Hulin, Elisabetta Antonioli, Xavier Leleu, Silvia Mangiacavalli, Aurore Perrot, Michele Cavo, Angelo Belotti, Annemiek Broijl, Francesca Gay, Roberto Mina, Niels W.C.J. van de Donk, Eirini Katodri
pmc-13178181.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryWhat is this summary about?This summary describes the first analysis of the PERSEUS study, which looked at adults with multiple myeloma that had never been treated before, also called newly diagnosed multiple myeloma. Multiple myeloma is a type of cancer in the blood, specifically in plasma cells within the soft, spongy tissue in the center of most bones, called the bone marrow.

pmc-13334730.title: Copper coordination polymer for multifunctional energy applications: hydrogen release, supercapacitor, and oxygen evolution reaction
pmc-13334730.creator: Zeinab Hussein Hashem, Laila H. Abdel-Rahman, Santiago Gómez-Ruiz, Hani Nasser Abdelhamid
pmc-13334730.description: The development of multifunctional materials for integrated energy conversion and storage is a critical challenge for sustainable energy solutions. A copper-based coordination polymer (Cu–BTEB) was synthesized by a reflux method using 4,4′,4″-(benzene-1,3,5-triyl)tris(ethyne-2,1-diyl)tribenzoic acid (H3BTEB) as the organic linker. The catalytic efficiency of Cu–BTEB for hydrogen production by NaBH4 hydrolysis exhibited a marked dependence on reactant concentration and temperature.

pmc-13340089.title: Genomic characterization of the emerging multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae ST6668 clone in northern Italy, 2020–2025
pmc-13340089.creator: Maryam Omrani, Virginia Batignani, Kiarash Moghaddasi, Arash Ghodousi, Stefano Gaiarsa, Aurora Piazza, Francesca Saluzzo, Daniela Maria Cirillo
pmc-13340089.description: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae carrying New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM) enzymes poses a major clinical and public health challenge due to their ability to spread rapidly in hospitals, and their resistance to most β-lactam antibiotics. Following the first report of the emerging NDM-producing K. pneumoniae lineage ST6668 in Pavia, Italy, we conducted a retrospective analysis at San Raffaele Hospital (Milan).

pmc-13421694.title: Gene regulatory innovations from transposable elements in primate cerebellum development
pmc-13421694.creator: Tetsuya Yamada, Mari Sepp, Ioannis Sarropoulos, Henrik Kaessmann
pmc-13421694.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Transposable elements are hypothesized to have driven gene regulatory innovation, yet their contributions to primate brain development at the cell type level remain underexplored. Here, we use single-cell multiomics data from human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse cerebella to show that transposable element contributions to different cell types are shaped by varying degrees of constraints across cell types, as well as the preferential co-option of certain transposable elements in specific cell states.

uslaw-usc-t18-s1545.title: 18 U.S.C. § 1545 — Safe conduct violation
uslaw-usc-t18-s1545.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s1545.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 75 (Passports And Visas). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever violates any safe conduct or passport duly obtained and issued under authority of the United States shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than 10 years, or both.

uslaw-usc-t43-s425b.title: 43 U.S.C. § 425b — Receipt of project water by lessees of irrigable lands owned by States, etc.; time limitation; applicability of acreage limitations
uslaw-usc-t43-s425b.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t43-s425b.description: United States Code, Title 43 (Public Lands); Chapter 12 (Reclamation And Irrigation Of Lands By Federal Government); Subchapter V (Administration Of Existing Projects). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Lessees of irrigable lands owned by States, political subdivisions, and agencies thereof which are held to be subject to the acreage limitation provisions of Federal reclamation law and for which recordable contracts to sell.
